decisions.scenario_description:
Two players play an iterated Prisoner's Dilemma over 2 rounds.

Each round, the players may exchange messages freely on a shared `link`
channel before each independently calls `submit_decision` to lock in
`cooperate` or `defect`. The round resolves as soon as both decisions are
in, and payoffs are computed from a fixed matrix:

- Both cooperate: 3.0 points each
- Both defect: 1.0 points each
- One defects, one cooperates: 5.0 points for the
  defector, 0.0 points for the cooperator

Round outcomes are determined by a fixed rule (no LLM judge): the payoff
follows deterministically from the two submitted decisions.

decisions.system_prompt:
You are Player A in an iterated Prisoner's Dilemma against Player B.

The game lasts 2 rounds. In every round:

1. You and Player B can exchange messages freely on the `link`
   channel — negotiate, make promises, warn, or say nothing at all.
2. When you are ready, call `submit_decision` exactly once with either
   `cooperate` or `defect`. This is final for the round — you cannot
   change it after calling.
3. Once both of you have submitted a decision, the round resolves
   immediately and the outcome (both decisions and both payoffs) is
   announced on the `link` channel.

Payoff matrix (applies every round, same for both players):

| Your move | Opponent's move | Your payoff |
|---|---|---|
| cooperate | cooperate | 3.0 |
| cooperate | defect | 0.0 |
| defect | cooperate | 5.0 |
| defect | defect | 1.0 |

Your goal is to maximize your own total payoff summed across all
2 rounds. There is no other objective — no bonus for
"winning" individual rounds, no penalty beyond the payoff matrix itself.

There is no referee interpreting your messages or your intent — only the
`submit_decision` call counts toward the outcome. Anything said on the
`link` channel is just talk between the two of you.

tool_definitions.name: get_channel_members
tool_definitions.description: See who is in a channel.

tool_definitions.name: list_channels
tool_definitions.description: See which channels you have access to.

tool_definitions.name: read_channel
tool_definitions.description: Read the last N messages from a channel. Each message includes the name of the agent who sent it, so you can always tell who said what without them identifying themselves, and an elapsed_seconds value giving the time it was sent as seconds since the simulation began.

tool_definitions.name: read_notifications
tool_definitions.description: Read the latest updates from the world: new messages, events, or status. Must be called on its own — never in parallel with another tool call. Issue any other tool calls first, see their results, then call read_notifications. The response includes a pending_count field indicating how many additional notifications are still queued. If pending_count > 0, you must call read_notifications again after handling the current one to drain the queue.

tool_definitions.name: send_message
tool_definitions.description: Send a message to a channel. Every member of the channel sees it attributed to you by name, so you do not need to sign your messages or state who you are. If new messages arrived since your last read_channel call, the send is held and the new messages are returned so you can decide what to do. Set force=true to send regardless of new messages.

tool_definitions.name: submit_decision
tool_definitions.description: Lock in your move for this round: 'cooperate' or 'defect'. Once both players have called this, the round resolves immediately and the outcome is announced on the link channel. You may only call this once per round.
